jobs.title: Research Services Clinical Sciences Program Manager
jobs.description:
University Staff

**Description**
---------------

**University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus**

**Department: Emergency Medicine**

**Job Title: Research Services Clinical Sciences Program Manager**

**Position #: 00853817 – Requisition #:** **41343**

**Job Summary:**

The University of Colorado, Anschutz Medical Campus, Department of Emergency Medicine is currently seeking applications for a Research Services Clinical Sciences Program Manager. This is a full-time, University Staff (non-classified) position for the Airway, Trauma, Lung injury, and Sepsis (ATLAS) Research Program.

Research Services Clinical Sciences Program Managers perform clinical and research-related functions which may include patient-oriented research or research conducted with human subjects. Patient-oriented research includes mechanisms of human disease, therapeutic interventions, clinical trials, or development of new technologies. Research Services Clinical Sciences Program Managers independently manage clinical research programs, perform clinical research project management functions and/or supervise clinical research teams of 2 or more FTE. This position will work closely with lead project coordinators, Principal Investigators (PIs), and ATLAS Leadership.

Key Responsibilities:

* Supervise research staff and coordinators.
* Provide leadership, direction, coaching, and performance management to professional staff.
* Develop protocol-specific systems and documents including process flows, training manuals, Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and Case Report Forms (CRFs). Maintains subject level documentation and prepares documents, equipment and/or supplies
* May perform supervision and management responsibilities for a team of 2 or more professionals. Duties include, but are not limited to, recruitment, supervision, and performance management responsibilities
* Manage project timelines, deliverables, and resources.
* Develop program/project goals and communicate goals and outcomes with a variety of stakeholders
* Participate in tactical and strategic program/project development and planning
* Coordinate site visits and other meetings with key stakeholders
* Develop and implement community outreach and engagement initiatives
* Assist with and oversee the day-to-day operations of clinical trials and studies, when needed
* May perform duties and responsibilities of Clinic Research Professionals when necessary
* Ensure compliance with FDA, IRB, and institutional requirements.
* Develop, review, maintain regulatory and other program/project documentation
* Ensure program/project compliance with Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and other regulatory bodies
* Support study activation, implementation, and closeout activities.
* Liaise and coordinate with a variety of program/project stakeholders including, but not limited to, program/project sponsors, regulatory agents, pharmaceutical representatives, and clinic/hospital staff
* Develop and maintain a variety of reports and communicate and present data to stakeholders

This description is a summary only and describes the general level of work being performed, it is not intended to be all-inclusive. The duties of this position may change from time to time and/or based on business needs. We reserve the right to add or delete duties and responsibilities at the discretion of the supervisor and/or hiring authority.

**Work Location:**

Hybrid – this role is eligible for a hybrid schedule of 4 days per week on campus and as needed for in-person meetings.

**Why Join Us:**

This is an in-person position within the ATLAS Research Program, which offers a unique career and growth opportunity to serve as an integral member of a highly productive, collaborative, and vibrant research group conducting impactful health research in the care of acutely ill and injured patients. The diverse and complex patient population provides a rich learning environment and opportunities to expand the candidate's skillset across several research projects (including clinical trials and observational trials). The candidate will also be exposed to a like-minded research community to help enrich skills and enhance career growth. The ATLAS Research Program aims to advance solutions to the greatest challenges in acute care by leading transformative clinical trials. We are interested in candidates that have/want a direct connection to advancing medical knowledge and evidence-based care that can impact the lives of patients.

Outside the ATLAS Research Program environment, the candidate will be part of the larger University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus community. CU Anschutz is a prestigious public education, clinical and research academic institution serving 4,500 students, and a world-class medical destination at the forefront of life-changing science, medicine, and healthcare. The campus encompasses the University of Colorado health professional schools, more than 60 centers and institutes, and two nationally ranked independent hospitals - UCHealth University of Colorado Hospital and Children's Hospital Colorado - that treat more than two million adult and pediatric patients each year. CU Anschutz offers more than 42 highly rated degree programs through 6 schools and colleges, and receives over $650 million in research awards each year. We are the single largest health professions education provider in Colorado, awarding nearly 1,450 degrees annually. Powered by our award-winning faculty, renowned researchers and a reputation for academic excellence, the CU Anschutz Medical Campus drives innovation from the classroom to the laboratory to the delivery of unparalleled patient care.

The University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus seeks individuals with demonstrated commitment to creating an inclusive learning and working environment. jobs.title: Clinician and Clinical Supervisor
jobs.description:
**SYNOPSIS**

The clinician will provide direct individual and group clinical services to residential and community clients served by TESSA in Douglas County. Services may include play-based therapeutic interventions as appropriate and within the clinician’s training and scope of practice. The clinician will also provide clinical supervision, training, and support to one to three master’s-level clinical interns, depending on program needs. The clinician will oversee the clinical intern recruitment and onboarding process in Douglas County and support the ongoing training and professional development needs of clinical interns. The clinician will serve as an integral member of TESSA’s Douglas County team and collaborate with TESSA’s broader Clinical Department.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Therapy Services**

* Provide trauma-informed individual and group clinical services to residential and community clients, including play-based therapeutic interventions as appropriate and within the clinician’s training and scope of practice.
* Complete required clinical assessments, treatment planning, documentation, and client records accurately and within established timelines.
* Maintain client confidentiality and comply with applicable legal, ethical, professional, and organizational requirements.
* Respond appropriately to client safety concerns, mandated reporting obligations, and other clinical risk-management needs in accordance with professional standards and TESSA policies.

**Clinical Internship Supervision, Training & Support**

* Provide clinical supervision, consultation, training, and support to assigned master’s-level clinical interns in accordance with applicable professional, regulatory, university, and organizational requirements.
* Provide weekly supervision and ongoing support and training to assigned clinical interns, including reviewing clinical documentation and coordinating with participating universities.
* Oversee the application and interview process for prospective clinical interns.
* Coordinate onboarding and orientation for accepted clinical interns.
* Provide training on TESSA’s clinical documentation and electronic health record systems.
* Coordinate and track required privacy, confidentiality, and compliance training for new clinical interns and staff members, as appropriate.
* Collaborate with the Volunteer Coordinator regarding Confidential Victim Advocate training and other required onboarding documentation.
* Assist with intern transition and completion activities at the conclusion of each internship.
* Research and coordinate ongoing training and professional development opportunities for clinical interns.
* Coordinate clinical in-service trainings and other learning opportunities.
* Provide additional individual training, consultation, and support based on identified needs.

**Program Evaluation & Quality Improvement**

* Create, update, and maintain tools for gathering client feedback regarding clinical services.
* Track and compile feedback from individual and group clinical services.
* Collect, maintain, and compile clinical service data for program evaluation, quality improvement, and grant reporting.
* Provide relevant client feedback, service data, and identified trends to clinicians, group facilitators, and program leadership to support continuous improvement.

**Cultural Responsiveness & Client Relations**

* Provide services in a manner that respects the dignity, experiences, identities, cultures, and individual needs of each client.
* Recognize and address personal assumptions and biases that may affect interactions, clinical decision-making, supervision, or service delivery.
* Demonstrate cultural humility and responsiveness when working with clients, interns, colleagues, volunteers, partner agencies, and community members from diverse backgrounds and lived experiences.
* Incorporate culturally responsive practices into clinical services, supervision, training, and professional development.
* Identify and work to reduce discriminatory or systemic barriers affecting access to services.
* Support organizational practices, policies, and procedures that promote equitable and culturally responsive services.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND REQUIREMENTS**

To perform this position successfully, an individual must be able to perform the essential functions satisfactorily. The qualifications below are representative of the knowledge, skills, abilities, and other requirements necessary for the position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

* Current, unrestricted Colorado licensure as a Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW), Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist (LMFT), or Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC), with the qualifications necessary to provide supervision to assigned master’s-level clinical interns in accordance with applicable professional, regulatory, university, and organizational requirements.
* Maintain all licenses, credentials, continuing education, and other professional requirements necessary to perform the clinical and supervisory functions of the position.
* Experience providing trauma-informed behavioral health services.
* Experience working with survivors of intimate partner violence, sexual violence, stalking, human trafficking, or other forms of interpersonal trauma preferred.
* Experience providing clinical supervision, consultation, or training to graduate-level interns preferred.
* Knowledge of professional ethics, confidentiality, mandated reporting, clinical documentation, and applicable legal and regulatory requirements.
* Excellent organizational, verbal and written communication, problem-solving, active-listening, and interpersonal skills.
* Strong attention to detail and the ability to provide empathetic, supportive, and nonjudgmental services while maintaining appropriate professional boundaries.
* Ability to manage multiple priorities and perform effe

jobs.title: Medical Social Worker
jobs.description:
Description:

Optimal Home Care is looking for a **Medical Social Worker** to provide services for our patients!

**About us:**

Optimal Hospice is devoted to helping our patients achieve and maintain the best possible quality of life. Our mission is to improve and restore our clients’ lives through quality patient care, innovative specialty health care programs and state of the art technology. The Optimal team embodies compassion, heart, patience, empathy, and competence to meet our patient’s needs.

**Core values:** Commitment Advocacy Respect Excellence

**Why Optimal Hospice?**

**Thriving Together:** As we grow, so does the opportunity for personal and professional advancement. Join a team that's not just about today but invested in building a future where your contributions make a lasting impact.

**Community of Care:** Optimal Hospice is more than an agency; it's a community dedicated to nurturing your skills and passions. We've crafted an environment that encourages growth and celebrates the unique strengths each team member brings.

**Heartfelt Connection:** In a world of growth and expansion, we've retained the warmth of a close-knit family. Your journey with Optimal Hospice is more than a career - it's a personal connection to a purpose-driven community.

**Position & Responsibilities:**

* Complies with ethical and professional standards of conduct as set forth by the National Association of Social Workers.
* Practices and maintains patient safety and dignity by abiding by Federal, State, Local and Optimal policy & procedures as pertains to patient protected health information and HIPAA (Health Information Portability and Accountability Act).
* Provides rehabilitative and supportive casework with the purpose of restoring patients to their optimum level of social and health adjustment. This includes assisting patients and their families to understand, accept and adhere to medical regimens.
* Assist patients and their families with personal and environmental difficulties which predispose them to illness and interfere with their obtaining maximum benefits from medical care.
* Prepares a social history and Plan of Care with the purpose of improving the scope and quality of existing services or extending services. When indicated, assists in the development of the Physician's Plan of Care.
* Assist patient and family to utilize existing resources in the home environment or refer patient and family to community agencies and act as an intermediary for the patient as necessary.
* Assess, when appropriate, a family's financial situation, taking into consideration the patient’s prognosis and medical needs and facilitating the referral process to any agency for financial assistance.
* Consults with the Physician and other members of the health team for the purpose of assisting them to understand significant social, emotional and environmental factors related to the patient’s health problems.
* Records clinical/progress notes in the patient’s clinical record weekly.

**Benefits:**

* Family Oriented Company
* Dedicated intake and scheduling team that support you and your patients
* Supportive work environment with opportunity to learn and develop
* Mileage reimbursement
* 401K plan
* Company phone provided
* Opportunity to provide individualized care to patients
* Continuing education opportunities

Requirements:

**Qualifications:**

* Degree in Social Work (Minimum of Bachelor's degree in Social Work or Psychology)
* LSW license in good standing in the State of Colorado
* Documented evidence of training in dealing with grief and loss.
* Hospice Experience (Required)
* Bachelor's in Psychology or Social Work
* Social Work License (Preferred)

### **Job Summary**

The Student Academic Success Center (SASC) at CU Boulder invites applications for The Program Manager – Scholarly Engagement and Post-Baccalaureate Success position! This is a part-time university staff position in the Student Academic Success Center (SASC) that supports a research-intensive learning program and assigned scholarly engagement initiatives. Reporting to the Program Director, this position serves on a three-member team that provides day-to-day oversight and operational support for the portfolio’s programs and services.

  
  

The Program Manager serves as the primary day-to-day coordinator for the Puksta Scholars Program, with direction from the Program Director, supports scholarly engagement and post-baccalaureate success initiatives across SASC. Responsibilities include recruitment and onboarding; advising and coaching; workshops, activities, and events; communications, records management, and assessment support; and coordination of student participation in high-impact scholarly engagement and post-baccalaureate preparation experiences.

  
  

This position helps implement upper-division programming in scholarly activity and civic learning; faculty mentorship and undergraduate research; fellowship applications and graduate or professional school preparation; and other enrichment experiences. The position coordinates assigned program processes; maintains effective working relationships with educational opportunity programs, campus offices, research faculty, and community partners; and recommends improvements based on student needs, success outcomes, and operational efficiencies. This position requires collegiality and professionalism; sound judgment and strong organization; initiative and problem-solving skills.

CU is an Equal Opportunity Employer and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment. We are committed to creating a workplace where all individuals are treated with respect and dignity, and we encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply, including protected veterans and individuals with disabilities.

### **Who We Are**

The Student Academic Success Center (SASC) is an educational opportunity center in the Office of Undergraduate Education within Academic Affairs at the University of Colorado Boulder. For more than 60 years, SASC has supported student success through a mission-inspired learning community of students, faculty, and staff whose backgrounds and pathways are historically non-traditional in higher education.

  
  

Within SASC, the Scholarly Engagement and Post-Baccalaureate portfolio comprises the McNair Scholars Program which serves 25 students engaged in undergraduate research, and the Puksta Scholars Program which serves 16 students engaged in community-based projects. Together, these two research-focused programs and expanded upper-division services contribute to the pre-college to post-baccalaureate pathway in SASC by advancing scholarly engagement, civic learning, and preparation for post-baccalaureate opportunities for our students.

### **What Your Key Responsibilities Will Be**

Program and Portfolio Operations

* Facilitates day-to-day operations for the Puksta Scholars Program and assigned portfolio initiatives across the academic year service cycle.
* Responsible for recruitment and outreach; application and selection; onboarding and orientation; and year-round engagement and retention of Puksta Scholars.
* Leads the Puksta Scholars Program plan of operations in collaboration with the Program Director, including advising support, enrichments, and student success initiatives.
* Coordinates program calendars, events, retreats, meetings, and workshops that support scholarly engagement, civic learning, academic achievement, and post-baccalaureate preparation.
* Serves as the primary operational contact for Puksta Scholars and coordinates routine communication, follow-up, referrals, and resolution of program questions.
* Supports new upper-division scholarly engagement initiatives by supporting logistics, materials, events, and other assigned components.
  

  
Student Engagement and Enrichment
  

* Provides high-contact student support that strengthens students’ academic, scholarly, civic, and post-baccalaureate development.
* Provides individualized advising, coaching, and developmental support to Puksta Scholars and students participating in assigned scholarly engagement initiatives.
* Helps students develop and monitor academic, scholarly, civic, leadership, research, and post-baccalaureate goals.
* Connects students with faculty mentors and research opportunities; scholarships and fellowships; graduate or professional preparation resources; career development, academic support, and other campus resources.
* Facilitates educational experiences and community-building activities that strengthen scholarly engagement, civic learning, belonging, leadership development, and post-baccalaureate preparation.
* Monitors student engagement, identifies barriers to persistence or participation, and coordinates with the Program Director appropriate interventions and referrals.

Assessment and Improvement

* Manages records, data collection, documentation, and reporting processes that support assessment, accountability, and continuous improvement.
* Maintains accurate student records, participation data, advising documentation, program files, calendars, handbooks, forms, resource materials, curricular or co-curricular materials, and assessment data in accordance with university or sponsor policies and program requirements.
* Facilitates collection of participation, engagement, satisfaction, academic progress, and outcome data for program and assigned scholarly en

jobs.title: Program Manager - Transportation
jobs.description:
**Department Information**
--------------------------

The mission of the Colorado Energy Office (CEO) is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and consumer energy costs by advancing clean energy, energy efficiency, and zero emission vehicles to benefit all Coloradans. We do this by developing and implementing highly impactful policies and programs, establishing Colorado as a leading state for climate action. The Colorado Energy Office is a great place to work, with collaborative and talented employees who are passionate about our mission and a hybrid atmosphere. Employees report high satisfaction with their work, their colleagues and manager, and CEO leadership. Join us!

  
  

Reducing greenhouse gas pollution and advancing zero emission vehicles, energy efficiency and clean energy are essential to preserving and protecting Colorado’s way of life. These actions defend the health of our communities and natural environment, provide access to lower cost clean energy resources for rural and urban areas, increase investment and economic growth opportunities, and expand clean energy jobs. As part of our mission we serve the people of Colorado with programs focusing on weatherization, energy efficiency, and electric vehicles and a regulatory and legislative agenda to promote the interests of all Coloradans.

  
  

This role will work on marketing, outreach by vendors, technical assistance efforts and administrative support related to CEO’s transportation electrification work.

  
  

***We are committed to increasing the diversity of our staff and providing culturally responsive programs and services. Therefore, we encourage responses from people of all backgrounds and abilities.***

  
  

The State of Colorado strives to create a Colorado for All by building and maintaining workplaces that value and respect all Coloradans through a commitment to equal opportunity and hiring based on merit and fitness. The State is resolute in non-discriminatory practices in everything we do, including hiring, employment, and advancement opportunities. Governor’s Office staff should demonstrate a commitment to equity, diversity, inclusion and accessibility (EDIA) in the workplace to fulfill the promise of a Colorado For All. Staff are expected to participate in learning opportunities and training to increase their knowledge around EDIA, have a growth mindset, and embed new learnings and skills into daily business practices. Creating inaccessible digital content such as web pages, emails, presentations, or documents leaves the state open to fines up to $3,500 based on the language in House Bill 21-110. Staff should strive to make all digital content accessible using provided accessibility resources.

**Description of Job**
----------------------

**Starting Salar****y Range:** **$70,012.80 - $90,001.60** **A****nnually**

* **This position is eligible for a hybrid remote working arrangement. Hybrid positions are expected to be present at the office location two full days per week, typically on the assigned team days, or as directed by their supervisor.**

General Duties and Responsibilities

* Electric Vehicle Marketing Program Lead

  + Lead the EV CO marketing program by selecting, onboarding, and managing CEO's new marketing vendor (anticipated start in early 2027).
  + Coordinate EV CO advisory and steering committees, facilitating regular meetings and collaboration.
  + Guide vendor in developing effective messaging and resources to encourage EV adoption across Colorado.
  + Serve as a subject matter expert on Colorado's EV market and vehicle electrification initiatives to keep content engaging, accurate, and aligned with market trends.
  + Oversee targeted marketing and outreach for specific transportation initiatives, including priority community engagement, the Community Connectors project, and Superusers program.
  + Manage vendor contracts, procurement, deliverables, invoices, performance, and budget tracking.
  + Use program data and analytics in partnership with the Program Analyst to evaluate outcomes, monitor efficacy, and drive continuous improvement.
  + Collaborate with Transportation team members and the Communications & Engagement team to align EV CO, ReCharge Colorado, and other outreach efforts.
  + Lead Colorado Electric Vehicle Coalition meetings and subgroups, establishing agendas and sustaining member engagement.
  + Respond to public inquiries regarding CEO programs and transportation electrification.
* Technical Assistance Lead

  + Lead technical assistance and advisory initiatives to support Transportation Team program managers and participants.
  + Identify technical assistance needs alongside program managers and stakeholders, managing contracts for key services such as fleet advising and multi-family housing support.
* Community Access Enterprise Board Support

  + Provide administrative support for the Board, including meeting logistics, agenda setting, speaker coordination, and facilitating public comment.
  + Ensure compliance with open meeting laws and oversee annual statutory reporting.
  + Maintain and update the Board's public-facing website.
* Provide additional support or leadership on other programs and purchase orders as assigned.

**Minimum Qualifications, Substitutions, Conditions of Employment & Appeal Rights**
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Minimum of three years professional experience in program or project management.
* Knowledge and experience with education, outreach and engagement
* Strong written, oral, and presentation communication skills.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Knowledge and experience with electric and zero emission vehicles, charging/fueling infrastructure programming, and/or fleets strongly preferred.
* Strong time management and organizational skills and the ability to manage a significant number of ongoing grants at various stages.
* High level of initiative

jobs.title: Patient Care Coordinator
jobs.description:
2CHealth Solutions is currently looking for a full-time Chronic Care Case Manager to join our growing organization. We specialize in care for patients with chronic diseases. Your primary duty would be to work remotely as a Case Manager. The Case Manager, who works as a Care Coordinator, is a trained healthcare professional who helps to address patients' concerns and manage their chronic diseases through Chronic Care Management (CCM), Principal Care Management (PCM), and Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) programs.

Responsibilities, but not limited to:

* Monitoring and coordinating treatment and care plans.
* Providing care management and coordination services through **CCM, PCM, and RPM** programs.
* Conducting patient outreach, follow-ups, and health assessments as required.
* Educating patients about their disease condition and helping them understand their care plans.
* Monitoring RPM data and identifying changes or concerns that may require follow-up or escalation.
* Connecting patients with healthcare providers, and evaluating their progress.
* Updating patient-related health information, insurance and financial information.
* Ensuring all immediate patient concerns and requests are being addressed.
* Assessing and developing healthcare interventions with the care team.
* Identifying gaps in care and coordinating appropriate follow-up and interventions.
* Documenting patient interactions, care coordination activities, patient enrollments, and encounters accurately and timely.
* Working in collaboration with other healthcare providers and care teams including behavioral health, disease care management, home health care, social work, and community-based organizations as needed.

Qualities of ideal applicant:

* Excellent communication skills
* Problem-solving - take initiative to solve problems that arise
* Well organized with attention to detail
* Time management
* Ability to work as a team member, anticipating providers needs in regards to patient care
* Empathetic with patients' needs and concerns
* Ability to work independently in a remote environment
* Strong documentation and follow-up skills

License, Education and Experience:

* Certified Nursing Assistant with appropriate experience
* Current Medical Assistant-Certified, Medical Healthcare Diploma
* 1 Year of professional experience in the same vicinity
* Experience in **CCM, PCM, RPM, care coordination, or a similar healthcare setting** is preferred

Compensation:

* **Productivity-based compensation**
* Earnings are based on completed and successfully documented patient enrollment/encounter activity.
* Additional incentives may be available based on productivity and performance.

Schedule:

* 8 hour shift

Education:

* High school or equivalent (Preferred)

Experience:

* CNA/MA: 1 year (Required)
* Chronic Care Management: 1 year (Required)
* Experience with CCM, PCM, or RPM preferred

Work Location:

Remote

Job Types:

Full-time, Part-time

Experience:

* CMA: 1 year (Preferred)

Language:

* Spanish (Required)

Pay: $10.00 - $30.00 per hour

Experience:

* PCM: 1 year (Required)

Language:

* Spanish (Preferred)

License/Certification:

* CMA/CNA (Required)

Work Location: Remote

### **Job Summary**

The Student Academic Success Center (SASC) at CU Boulder invites applications for The Program Manager – Scholarly Engagement and Post-Baccalaureate Success position! This is a part-time university staff position in the Student Academic Success Center (SASC) that supports a research-intensive learning program and assigned scholarly engagement initiatives. Reporting to the Program Director, this position serves on a three-member team that provides day-to-day oversight and operational support for the portfolio’s programs and services.

  
  

The Program Manager serves as the primary day-to-day coordinator for the Puksta Scholars Program, with direction from the Program Director, supports scholarly engagement and post-baccalaureate success initiatives across SASC. Responsibilities include recruitment and onboarding; advising and coaching; workshops, activities, and events; communications, records management, and assessment support; and coordination of student participation in high-impact scholarly engagement and post-baccalaureate preparation experiences.

  
  

This position helps implement upper-division programming in scholarly activity and civic learning; faculty mentorship and undergraduate research; fellowship applications and graduate or professional school preparation; and other enrichment experiences. The position coordinates assigned program processes; maintains effective working relationships with educational opportunity programs, campus offices, research faculty, and community partners; and recommends improvements based on student needs, success outcomes, and operational efficiencies. This position requires collegiality and professionalism; sound judgment and strong organization; initiative and problem-solving skills.

CU is an Equal Opportunity Employer and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment. We are committed to creating a workplace where all individuals are treated with respect and dignity, and we encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply, including protected veterans and individuals with disabilities.

### **Who We Are**

The Student Academic Success Center (SASC) is an educational opportunity center in the Office of Undergraduate Education within Academic Affairs at the University of Colorado Boulder. For more than 60 years, SASC has supported student success through a mission-inspired learning community of students, faculty, and staff whose backgrounds and pathways are historically non-traditional in higher education.

  
  

Within SASC, the Scholarly Engagement and Post-Baccalaureate portfolio comprises the McNair Scholars Program which serves 25 students engaged in undergraduate research, and the Puksta Scholars Program which serves 16 students engaged in community-based projects. Together, these two research-focused programs and expanded upper-division services contribute to the pre-college to post-baccalaureate pathway in SASC by advancing scholarly engagement, civic learning, and preparation for post-baccalaureate opportunities for our students.

### **What Your Key Responsibilities Will Be**

Program and Portfolio Operations

* Facilitates day-to-day operations for the Puksta Scholars Program and assigned portfolio initiatives across the academic year service cycle.
* Responsible for recruitment and outreach; application and selection; onboarding and orientation; and year-round engagement and retention of Puksta Scholars.
* Leads the Puksta Scholars Program plan of operations in collaboration with the Program Director, including advising support, enrichments, and student success initiatives.
* Coordinates program calendars, events, retreats, meetings, and workshops that support scholarly engagement, civic learning, academic achievement, and post-baccalaureate preparation.
* Serves as the primary operational contact for Puksta Scholars and coordinates routine communication, follow-up, referrals, and resolution of program questions.
* Supports new upper-division scholarly engagement initiatives by supporting logistics, materials, events, and other assigned components.
  

  
Student Engagement and Enrichment
  

* Provides high-contact student support that strengthens students’ academic, scholarly, civic, and post-baccalaureate development.
* Provides individualized advising, coaching, and developmental support to Puksta Scholars and students participating in assigned scholarly engagement initiatives.
* Helps students develop and monitor academic, scholarly, civic, leadership, research, and post-baccalaureate goals.
* Connects students with faculty mentors and research opportunities; scholarships and fellowships; graduate or professional preparation resources; career development, academic support, and other campus resources.
* Facilitates educational experiences and community-building activities that strengthen scholarly engagement, civic learning, belonging, leadership development, and post-baccalaureate preparation.
* Monitors student engagement, identifies barriers to persistence or participation, and coordinates with the Program Director appropriate interventions and referrals.

Assessment and Improvement
